newsitem.title: CANADA: Chevron Canada assets may merge with NGC.
newsitem.headline: Chevron Canada assets may merge with NGC.

text.p: The extensive natural gas gathering and processing assets of Chevron Corp's Canadian subsidiary may be merged with energy marketer NGC Corp of Houston, a Chevron Canada executive said on Monday.

Calgary-based Chevron Canada Resources' midstream gas assets were excluded from a merger deal in the United States, in which Chevron Corp's Warren and Chevron USA units, which market and process gas and gas liquids, were folded into NGC.
The deal created North America's biggest integrated energy marketer.

But a recent move by NGC and Calgary-based NOVA Corp -- an NGC owner -- to split up their co-owned Novagas Clearinghouse unit has made executives at Chevron take a second look at integrating Chevron Canada's gas and gas liquids operations into NGC, said Wayne Scott, Chevron Canada's vice-president of marketing.

"I know, for us, we have re-opened negotiations with NGC, primarily because we had 28 percent of a 50 percent interest (in Novagas). Now we have 28 of 100 percent interest in the entity we do business with in Canada," Scott told Reuters following a presentation to a natural gas conference.

NOVA and NGC, amid pressure from Canadian producers, said last month they would split Novagas into three, with NOVA owning 100 percent of gas aggregator unit Pan-Alberta Gas and the operation's midstream assets, and NGC owning 100 percent of its gas marketing business, to be renamed NGC Canada.
"There is better corporate economics to do something more with (NGC)," he said. "But whether it's a merger or just expanding commercial operations, we haven't decided yet."
Chevron Corp, NOVA and British Gas Plc each own 24 percent of NGC's common shares. Chevron also holds an extra four percent non-voting stake.
While not part of the Chevron-NGC merger, Chevron Canada has an exclusive commercial arragement with the Houston-based company.

Ironically, if a merger went ahead, NGC would compete in Canada with part-owner NOVA in the midstream business. Over the past few years, Novagas expanded its unregulated Canadian gas gathering processing business and entered the gas liquids industry earlier this year.
Even now, competition exists, Scott said.

"Right now, it's kind of amusing because three companies, Chevron, NGC and NOVA -- all interconnected -- are basically competing in their own names in Canada, and that's not the case in the U.S," he said. -- Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
